key_equations_and_data: §3.1 energy-form Planck: B(λ,T) = C1L / (λ^5 (exp(C2/(λT)) − 1)), λ in µm, B in W·m⁻²·sr⁻¹·µm⁻¹; C1L = 2hc² = 1.19104297e8 W·µm⁴·m⁻²·sr⁻¹ (constants.C1L, exists)

§3.1 photon-form Planck: B_q(λ,T) = C1Q / (λ^4 (exp(C2/(λT)) − 1)), ph·s⁻¹·m⁻²·sr⁻¹·µm⁻¹; C1Q = 2c = 5.995849e26 (constants.C1Q, exists). Mandatory for photon detectors (MWIR/SWIR/NIR, §9.1); energy form for bolometers (§9.2)
§3.1/§16.3 C2 = hc/k_B = 1.4387769e4 µm·K; σ = 5.670374419e-8 W·m⁻²·K⁻⁴; Wien λ_max·T = 2897.771955 µm·K; h, c, k_B, q exact CODATA 2018 (all exist in constants.py)
§3.1 known answers: B(10 µm, 300 K) = 9.924 W·m⁻²·sr⁻¹·µm⁻¹ (I get 9.92403); B_q = 4.996e20 (I get 4.99587e20); B_q·hc/λ = B to 1e-12 rel; M = σT⁴, Lambertian L = σT⁴/π; 300 K peaks at 9.66 µm

§3.2(a) fractional exitance F_{0→λT} = (15/π⁴) Σ_n e^{−nx}/n (x³ + 3x²/n + 6x/n² + 6/n³), x = C2/(λT); L_B = (σT⁴/π)[F(λ₂T) − F(λ₁T)] for a top-hat response (exists: fractional_exitance, band_radiance_tophat; scalar only)

NOT IN SPEC but required as an independent oracle for the photon LUT: photon fractional exitance F_q(x) = (1/(2ζ(3))) Σ_n e^{−nx}(x²/n + 2x/n² + 2/n³); M_q = σ_q T³ with σ_q = 2π·2ζ(3)·k_B³/(h³c²) = 1.52046e15 ph·s⁻¹·m⁻²·K⁻³ (verified numerically: Lb/Lb_q for 7.5–13.5 µm at 300 K gives λ_eff = 10.4 µm). σ_q must be added to constants.py with this derivation as its source

§3.2 band radiance by quadrature: L_B(T) = ∫ R(λ) B(λ,T) dλ, Simpson on a 0.01 µm grid; R(λ) normalised to peak 1.0 (ir-radiometry skill lines 133–135; §2 symbol table: R = QE × filter × window, normalised). Same for L_{q,B}, (∂L/∂T)_B, (∂L_q/∂T)_B

§3.2(b) LUT: uniform T grid [200, 1000] K at 0.05 K → 16001 entries, float32, 64 004 bytes per quantity per band; linear interpolation in T. Quantities: Lb, Lb_q, dLb_dT (skill) PLUS dLb_q_dT (required by §9.4 photon NETD, missing from skill/script)
§3.3 apparent temperature T_app = L_B⁻¹(L_measured); L_B monotonic → binary search on the same LUT (or stored inverse). T_kinetic vs T_apparent naming must be kept distinct

§3.4 thermal derivative ∂B/∂T = B · C2/(λT²) · e^x/(e^x − 1) (exists, energy form; implemented as 1 + 1/expm1(x)); photon analogue ∂B_q/∂T = B_q · C2/(λT²) · e^x/(e^x − 1) (MISSING); in-band (∂L/∂T)_B = ∫ R ∂B/∂T dλ tabulated alongside L_B

§3.4 [R9] NETD anchor: uncooled core ≈39 mK at ambient → ≈23 mK at 100 °C. Verified: (∂L_B/∂T)(373 K)/(∂L_B/∂T)(300 K) = 1.736 for 7.5–13.5 µm (1.750 for 8–12 µm) → 39/1.736 = 22.5 mK. A known-answer test for the in-band derivative
§9.4 photon-count NETD = σ_N,total / (∂N_e/∂T), ∂N_e/∂T = η A_d t_int π τ_opt/(4F²+1) · (∂L_q/∂T)_B — consumer of the dLb_q_dT table; §9.2 bolometer NETD uses (∂L/∂T)_B energy form

§13.3 temperature encoding c = (T − T_ref)/T_span, T_ref = 200 K, T_span = 800 K, float32 → the LUT range [200, 1000] K must equal [T_ref, T_ref + T_span]; fp16 spacing at 300 K = 0.25 K (non-negotiable #2)

§13.5 GPU LUT contract the CPU reference must mirror exactly: planckLUT[N] float32, lutT0, lutT1; u = (T − T0)/(T1 − T0)·(N − 1); u clamped to [0, N − 1.001]; i0 = int(u), fr = u − i0; L = lut[i0](1 − fr) + lut[i0+1]·fr. Sidecar JSON must carry N, T0, T1

§12.2 config fields consumed here: sensor.name (LUT file stem), sensor.band.lambda_min_um, sensor.band.lambda_max_um, sensor.band.spectral_response (CSV path), sensor.band.regime (emissive|reflective|mixed), sensor.fpa.type (bolometer|photon → which Planck form downstream, but generate all four tables regardless so bands stay data)

§15 Tier-1 tolerances owned by this area: photon vs energy form 1e-12 rel; ∫B dλ = σT⁴/π to 1e-6; LUT vs direct quadrature < 5 mK equivalent over 200–1000 K; L_B⁻¹(L_B(T)) = T < 1 mK; ∂L/∂T vs finite difference < 1e-5 rel; quadrature vs closed-form top-hat < 0.1 % (skill line 76); GPU vs CPU 1e-4 rel or 5 mK (testing skill)

Error budget facts for tolerance design: max linear-interpolation error on a 0.05 K grid is ≤ 0.03 mK (worst case SWIR 0.9–1.7 µm at 300 K; 0.003 mK for LWIR at 300 K) so any LUT-vs-quadrature disagreement above ~0.1 mK is a bug; float32 ulp of Lb at 300 K LWIR ≈ 4 µK; 0.1 % of Lb(7.5–13.5, 300 K) ≈ 63 mK, so the 0.1 % top-hat cross-check and the 5 mK LUT check are NOT interchangeable; a half-cell (0.005 µm) top-hat edge misalignment on the 0.01 µm grid ≈ 0.08 % ≈ 50 mK

work_items.title: Band-weighted spectral averaging for grey-within-band material properties
spec_refs: Appendix A #3 'Emissivity is grey within a band'
work_items.description: band_average(band, spectrum_lambda, T_ref) = ∫ R(λ) s(λ) B(λ,T_ref) dλ / ∫ R(λ) B(λ,T_ref) dλ (energy form; photon-weighted variant for photon detectors). This is the only sanctioned way for the materials area to reduce ε(λ), ρ(λ), τ(λ) files to per-band scalars. Linear in s, so Kirchhoff closure survives the reduction. Needs an ADR on the reference temperature (300 K fixed vs T-dependent table) because the weighted average of a sloped ε(λ) shifts with T.

decisions_needing_adr.title: Band LUT grid, precision and out-of-range policy
decisions_needing_adr.why: Fixes the temperature range every other stage (encoding §13.3, GPU kernel §13.5, thermal solver outputs, sky temperatures) must respect; the clamp behaviour silently saturates flares/exhaust above the top and cold sky below the bottom; the choice outlives the commit and must match the CUDA kernel bit-for-bit.
options: [200, 1000] K at 0.05 K, float32, linear interpolation, clamp at both ends (matches §13.3 encoding and the §13.5 kernel sketch exactly; 16001 entries, 64 kB per table)
[200, 1000] K at 0.1 K (8001 entries; interpolation error still ≤ 0.12 mK) — half the memory, no measurable accuracy cost
Wider range e.g. [150, 1500] K to cover winter clear-sky (T_air − 70 K) and exhaust manifolds, at the cost of changing T_ref/T_span in §13.3 and the encoding round-trip test
NaN or raise instead of clamp outside the range (safer in the CPU reference, but the GPU kernel clamps, so parity tests would disagree at the edges)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Inverse (apparent temperature) method
decisions_needing_adr.why: §3.3 allows binary search on the forward table or a stored inverse; the choice determines whether the < 1 mK round trip is exact-by-construction or limited by a second interpolation, and what the GPU IrApparentT stage must implement.
options: searchsorted + linear inversion inside the bin on the same float32 forward table (exact inverse of the piecewise-linear forward function; round trip limited only by float32; 14 iterations per pixel on GPU)
Precomputed inverse table on a uniform radiance grid (one gather per pixel, but radiance spans 3 decades between 200 K and 1000 K so a uniform grid is either huge or coarse at the cold end)
Newton iteration seeded from a coarse inverse (fast, but a second code path to validate)

decisions_needing_adr.title: LUT artefacts: committed vs generated, and on-disk format
decisions_needing_adr.why: The ir-radiometry skill says LUTs are checked into data/lut with a config hash; .gitignore ignores data/lut/*.npy and *.json. Which is true determines whether tests and the Isaac glue can assume the files exist, whether bit-reproducibility across numpy versions matters, and what the SPG Lua launch script can load.
options: Commit the .npy + .json (64 kB × 4 per band; remove the .gitignore lines; golden-style tolerance comparison on regeneration because float64 quadrature is not guaranteed bitwise across numpy/BLAS versions)

Never commit; `make luts` is part of `make install` and unit tests build LUTs on the fly from top-hat/synthetic bands (fast: < 2 s) — the Isaac side must run make luts before first use and check the hash
Commit only the sidecar JSON (hash + parameters) and regenerate arrays lazily with a cache keyed by the hash

Format: .npy + JSON sidecar (Python/Warp path reads natively) vs additionally a raw little-endian float32 .bin for the SPG Lua cuda.static upload — depends on what the Lua runtime can read (unverified)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Spectral response semantics and quadrature rule
decisions_needing_adr.why: R(λ) normalisation (peak 1, QE excluded and living in the detector model — or QE folded in as §9.1 permits), the resampling rule (linear interpolation to 0.01 µm, zero outside support), precedence between config lambda_min/max and CSV support, and Simpson (numpy composite vs scipy.integrate.simpson) are all silent multiplicative factors if two modules assume differently. The 5 mK LUT tolerance only means something if every consumer uses the same R(λ).
options: R(λ) is a peak-1 shape only; η (QE) lives in fpa config and is applied in the detector (recommended: keeps the LUT band-only and the config field 'quantum_efficiency' meaningful)

R(λ) includes QE × filter × window as §2's symbol table literally says, then normalised — η still needed separately for absolute photon counts, so the LUT and detector must agree on where the absolute scale lives
Config range clips CSV support (and the loader errors if the CSV is narrower) vs CSV support wins and the config range is documentation only
Composite Simpson in numpy on an edge-aligned odd-length grid (5 lines, inspectable) vs scipy.integrate.simpson (handles even N with a correction that changes results at the 1e-6 level)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Grey-within-band emissivity reduction (fidelity level deliberately skipped: §3.2(c) runtime quadrature)
decisions_needing_adr.why: Appendix A #3 accepts grey ε per band; the reduction from a spectral ε(λ) file to a scalar needs a weighting (R·B at some T) and the answer depends on T. Choosing T_ref = 300 K introduces a bounded but non-zero error for hot targets and for materials with sloped ε (quartz reststrahlen, vegetation); this is exactly the 'cheaper approximation on purpose' the ADR process exists for.
options: Weight by R(λ)·B(λ, 300 K) once per material per band (simplest; error for a 600 K exhaust with sloped ε can be checked with the R-05 T-dependence test)
Tabulate ε_B(T) per material per band on the same 200–1000 K grid (one more small LUT per material; exact for grey-body self-emission, still approximate for reflected terms)
Per-pixel runtime quadrature (hyperspectral fidelity; rejected by §3.2(c) for an imaging camera)

decisions_needing_adr.title: numpy version floor (dependency)
decisions_needing_adr.why: tests use np.trapezoid, present only in numpy ≥ 2.0, while pyproject declares numpy>=1.24; raising the floor is a dependency decision affecting the Isaac Sim 6.0 Python environment, whose bundled numpy version is unverified.
options: Raise to numpy>=2.0 (simplest; verify Isaac Sim 6.0's bundled numpy is ≥ 2.0 first)
Keep 1.24 floor and use a compat shim (np.trapezoid if present else np.trapz)
Avoid trapezoid entirely in tests by using the closed-form series and Simpson

decisions_needing_adr.title: Estimated Boson VOx spectral response
decisions_needing_adr.why: The real Boson R(λ) is not public; whatever curve is authored becomes the absolute radiometric calibration of the LWIR camera until a measured curve replaces it. Its provenance and the expected error must be recorded so nobody mistakes it for data.
options: Synthetic 7.5–13.5 µm top-hat with ~0.5 µm cosine roll-offs (documented as ESTIMATED; hash-tagged so replacing it invalidates every LUT)
Digitised typical VOx + Ge/AR curves from literature (better shape, still not this unit)
Pure top-hat (simplest, worst edge behaviour; §3.2(a) says ~1 % error for uncooled cores)

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The dev environment has never run the gate: miniconda Python 3.13 has no numpy/pytest/ruff/mypy, no .venv exists, and the single commit predates any CI. The CHANGELOG's 'analytic identity tests passing' is unverified in this checkout; mypy --strict on planck.py (FloatArray typing with scalar T) and ruff NPY rules may already fail.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: make install && make check on a Python 3.10–3.13 interpreter; record the outcome in R-00's commit body. Also pip install 'numpy<2' on Python 3.10 and run pytest to confirm the np.trapezoid AttributeError.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Spectral response file location is defined three different ways: spec §12.2 line 832 'responses/boson_vox.csv', the checked-in YAML line 13 'spectra/boson_vox.csv', the ir-radiometry skill line 121 'data/spectra/<detector>.csv'; and nothing states what the path is relative to (Makefile passes no data root). data/spectra/ will also hold material ε(λ) files (§12.3 'spectra/car_paint_black.csv'), which use a different normalisation (physical 0–1, not peak-1).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide in R-03's ADR (relative to data/, detector files under data/spectra/); add a loader test that a material-style file (peak 0.9) is rejected by the detector-response loader; fix the spec line or the YAML so they agree.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: CSV format for R(λ) is unspecified: delimiter, header lines, column order, whether λ may be descending, duplicate λ, and what to do outside the tabulated support. Any of these silently change Lb by percent-level amounts.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Write the format down in the loader docstring and the CSV header; R-03 tests for descending/nm/peak≠1; compare Lb from a hand-written top-hat CSV against band_radiance_tophat to 0.1 %.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Precedence between config lambda_min_um/lambda_max_um and the R(λ) CSV support is undefined. If the CSV extends beyond the config range (e.g. 7.0–14.0 µm) and the config range clips it, Lb differs by several percent from the unclipped integral.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: R-03 ADR decision plus a test: same CSV with two config ranges gives Lb values that differ exactly by band_radiance_tophat over the excluded interval (if clipping) or are identical (if the CSV wins).

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Out-of-range temperatures are real, not hypothetical: §5.3 gives T_sky = T_air − 55…70 K, so a −13 °C winter night puts zenith sky at ~190 K, below the 200 K LUT floor; §3.1 mentions 1000 K flares and exhaust manifolds exceed 1000 K. The §13.5 kernel clamps silently. If the sky radiance is computed through the LUT, cold-sky reflections on car roofs are wrong on exactly the nights the phenomenology checklist tests.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Compute L_sky on the CPU via the quadrature path (R-04), not the LUT, and add a test that band_radiance(190 K) ≠ lookup(190 K); decide in the LUT ADR whether to widen the range (and correspondingly T_ref/T_span in §13.3).

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Tolerance non-equivalence trap: the skill's '0.1 % on a top-hat' and the spec's '< 5 mK' differ by an order of magnitude (0.1 % of Lb at 300 K LWIR ≈ 63 mK). A team member could 'satisfy' the 5 mK LUT test by comparing against the closed-form top-hat at 0.1 %, which proves nothing about the LUT. Conversely, a half-cell edge misalignment on the 0.01 µm grid is ~50 mK, so a top-hat oracle test at 5 mK fails for grid reasons, not physics.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: R-04 uses the 0.1 % top-hat check with an edge-aligned grid; R-06 uses the 5 mK check against R-04's quadrature at off-grid T; both tests print the error in mK (via dLb_dT) so reviewers can see which regime they are in.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Which quantities to tabulate disagrees between spec and skill: §3.4 tabulates (∂L/∂T)_B; §9.4's photon-count NETD needs (∂L_q/∂T)_B; the skill (line 65) and the script docstring list only Lb, Lb_q, dLb_dT. Omitting dLb_q_dT forces the detector area to finite-difference the Lb_q table, a second implementation of the same derivative.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Include dLb_q_dT in R-06/R-08; test that the finite difference of the Lb_q table agrees with the dLb_q_dT table to 1e-4 relative, so a consumer using either gets the same NETD.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: SPG Lua asset loading is unverified for Isaac Sim 6.0: the spec (§13.5 note line 1111) says 'generate the LUT offline and load it as a binary asset' but neither the spec nor the isaac-sim-spg skill shows a Lua file-read or which formats cuda.array accepts; .npy has a header the Lua side would have to parse. The Warp/annotator path (§13.6, 'start here') reads .npy natively, so this only blocks the later SPG port.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Small experiment in Isaac Sim 6.0 with --enable omni.rtx.spg: attempt to read a raw float32 .bin in the .cu.lua via Lua io and pass through cuda.array inside cuda.static; if it works, R-08 also writes <sensor>_Lb.f32 next to the .npy. Belongs to the isaac area but decides R-08's format.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: R(λ) normalisation vs quantum efficiency: §2's symbol table defines R as 'QE × filter × window, normalised', §9.1 says η may be 'folded into R(λ) if you prefer', the YAML has a separate fpa.quantum_efficiency field, and the skill says 'absolute responsivity lives in the detector model'. Folding η into R and also applying fpa.quantum_efficiency double-counts it; not folding it but omitting the field under-counts photons.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide in the R-03 ADR (R is peak-1 shape; η applied once in the detector); add a detector-area test that photoelectron count for a flat QE equals η × A_d × t_int × Ω × Lb_q from the LUT.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: CPU/GPU parity depends on replicating float32 index arithmetic exactly: the kernel computes u = (T − T0)/(T1 − T0)·(N − 1) in float32 and clamps to N − 1.001. A CPU reference using float64 or np.interp will differ by up to one float32 ulp in u, which is harmless (< 1 µK) but a CPU reference that raises or extrapolates at the edges will disagree with the kernel by whole kelvins at 199 K/1001 K.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: R-06 implements the kernel's formula in float32 and tests exact equality at 199 K/200 K and 1000 K/1001 K; the isaac area's Warp parity test then compares at 1e-4 relative or 5 mK over the gbuffer_ramp fixture.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Unit-suite time budget (< 30 s total): building a 16001-point LUT from a 601-point λ grid is ~10 M Planck evaluations per quantity (fast in vectorised numpy, ~0.5 s), but fractional_exitance is a scalar Python loop — cross-checking all 16001 temperatures with it takes seconds. Naive tests will blow the budget and people will stop running the suite.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Session-scoped LUT fixture; top-hat cross-checks at ≤ 200 sampled temperatures; time the suite in CI (pytest --durations=10) and keep radiometry under 5 s.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: LUT determinism across numpy/BLAS/platform versions is not guaranteed at the bit level (float64 exp/expm1 differ in the last ulp between libm implementations), so a committed .npy compared bitwise will 'fail' on another machine while being physically identical.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: If LUTs are committed (R-08 ADR), compare on regeneration with a 0.1 mK tolerance, never bitwise; record the numpy version in the sidecar.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Grey-band emissivity reference temperature (R-05) is unspecified anywhere in the spec; Appendix A only says ε is grey within a band. For sloped ε(λ) (vegetation, quartz) the 300 K-weighted average applied to a 600 K target is wrong by an amount the spec does not bound.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: R-05's T-dependence test quantifies the shift for a representative sloped ε; the ADR either bounds it (< 0.5 % of ε for the material library) or chooses the ε_B(T) table option.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Simpson requires an odd number of uniformly spaced points; a band from 7.5 to 13.5 µm at 0.01 µm gives 601 points (odd, fine) but 0.9–1.7 µm gives 81 (fine) and arbitrary config ranges can give even counts. scipy.integrate.simpson silently applies an even-N correction; a hand-rolled Simpson may silently drop the last interval.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: R-04 asserts odd length (grid constructed with N = round(span/0.01) + 1, adjusting if even) and the top-hat integral test checks ∫R dλ == span to 1e-12.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free core: every module added here (band.py, band_integration.py, lut.py, and scripts/generate_luts.py's imports) is pure numpy (+ optional scipy); tests/unit/test_layering.py parametrises over src/irsim/**/*.py so new files are checked automatically — nothing extra to write, but the LUT-loading side for SPG/Warp must live in src/irsim_isaac and import from irsim.radiometry, never the reverse.

#2 float32 or better wherever temperature/radiance flows: LUT tables are float32 (built in float64, cast once); BandLUT.lookup/apparent_temperature assert input dtype ∉ {float16} and return float32 (R-06/R-07 tests: float16 input raises; gbuffer_ramp float32 in → float32 out); load_band_lut asserts float32 on every .npy (R-08 test: hand-written float16/float64 file rejected); the LUT range [200, 1000] K is pinned to §13.3's T_ref/T_span so the encode/decode round trip (isaac area, < 10 mK) and the LUT cover the same interval.

#3 Noise in radiance/electron space, never Kelvin: radiometry adds no noise but is what makes the rule enforceable — it must publish dLb_dT and dLb_q_dT tables so the noise area converts σ_radiance ↔ mK per pixel at the local temperature. Tests: existing test_thermal_derivative_rises_with_temperature plus R-04's known-answer ratio 1.736 (39 mK → 22.5 mK) and R-06's positive, increasing dLb_dT table. Any Kelvin-space noise shortcut would show up as a flat NETD in the Tier-2 bench, which these tables make detectable.

#4 Kirchhoff closure ε + ρ + τ = 1 to 1e-6: touched only through R-05 band averaging, which must be linear so closure survives the spectral → grey reduction; R-05 test asserts band_average(ε) + band_average(ρ) + band_average(τ) = 1 to 1e-9 for pointwise-closed spectra. The material-library walk test itself belongs to the materials area.

#5 Aperture factor π/(4F²+1) defined once in irsim.optics: radiometry must contain NO aperture, F-number, or π/(4F²) factor — Lb is radiance (W·m⁻²·sr⁻¹), not focal-plane irradiance; docstring first lines state units so a reviewer can catch a stray π. Verified by the Stefan-Boltzmann identity (L = σT⁴/π) and by unit-labelled return types; a grep for 'f_number' or '4 *' in src/irsim/radiometry should stay empty.

#6 One WeatherSeries for thermal and atmosphere: not touched by radiometry; the sky-temperature → L_sky conversion (§5.3) consumes R-04/R-06 but takes T_sky as an input from the thermal/atmosphere side, so radiometry has no weather dependency to get wrong.
spec_internal_inconsistencies: Spectral response path: docs/physics-model.md §12.2 line 832 says `responses/boson_vox.csv`; configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml line 13 says `spectra/boson_vox.csv`; .claude/skills/ir-radiometry/SKILL.md line 121 says `data/spectra/<detector>.csv`. No document states the base directory; Makefile line for `luts` passes only --configs and --out.
LUT artefacts committed vs ignored: ir-radiometry skill lines 65–66 'checked into data/lut/ with a hash of the config'; .gitignore lines 12–13 ignore data/lut/*.npy and data/lut/*.json.

Stefan-Boltzmann tolerance is stated three ways: spec §15 line 1178 and ir-radiometry skill line 107 say 1e-6; ir-sim-testing skill line 52 says 1e-12 relative for 'Analytic identities (Planck forms, Stefan-Boltzmann)'; tests/unit/test_planck.py line 42 asserts 2e-5 with a comment attributing the residual to tail truncation beyond 1000 µm (which is ~6e-6 at 300 K, so 1e-6 is unattainable by that method without the analytic tail). 1e-12 is only meaningful for the closed-form series (fractional_exitance → 1), not for quadrature.

Tables to tabulate: spec §3.4 line 188 tabulates (∂L/∂T)_B alongside L_B; spec §9.4 line 671 needs (∂L_q/∂T)_B for photon detectors; ir-radiometry skill line 65 and scripts/generate_luts.py docstring line 11 list only {Lb, Lb_q, dLb_dT}. The photon-form derivative (spectral and in-band) exists nowhere in code.

Wavelength plausibility bound: ir-radiometry skill line 38 says assert 0.1–100 µm and monotonic increasing; src/irsim/radiometry/constants.py line 50 sets WAVELENGTH_MAX_UM = 1000.0 (required by the Stefan-Boltzmann test integrating to 1000 µm) and planck._validate (lines 37–55) checks no monotonicity.

numpy floor vs API: pyproject.toml line 11 `numpy>=1.24`; tests/unit/test_planck.py lines 37, 64–65, 80 use np.trapezoid, which exists only in numpy ≥ 2.0 (np.trapz before). On the allowed numpy 1.x the suite errors.

LUT spacing: spec §3.2(b) line 164 '0.05–0.1 K'; ir-radiometry skill line 64, scripts/generate_luts.py line 9, and the CLAUDE.md/ship-step commit examples all say 0.05 K. Harmless, but pick one in the ADR.
Makefile `golden-update` target (line 27) passes `--update-golden`, which no conftest defines; pytest will reject the unknown option. ir-sim-testing skill line 108 presumes it works.

README line 'Bands configured: _none yet_' while configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml fully configures the LWIR band (only its spectral CSV is missing); README status row for radiometry claims T1 but the T1 rows in §15 that belong to radiometry (LUT vs quadrature, inverse round trip) do not exist.

CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #2 says 'There is a test for the encode/decode round trip; keep it passing' and the isaac-sim-spg skill line 112 names tests/integration/test_temperature_encoding.py; tests/integration/ contains only .gitkeep. (Isaac area, but the LUT range decision here must match that future test's T_ref/T_span.)

Out-of-range temperature behaviour: spec §13.5 kernel (line 1057) clamps T to the LUT range silently, while §3.1 line 144 cites 1000 K flares (exactly the LUT top) and §5.3 line 311 yields sky temperatures below 200 K on cold clear nights; §3.3 gives no policy for radiance outside the table on inversion. planck._validate's TEMPERATURE bounds (1–6000 K) are far wider than the LUT, so the reference and fast paths will diverge silently unless a policy is written.

Fail-loud philosophy is applied inconsistently in existing code: planck.spectral_radiance/_photon_radiance/d_spectral_radiance_dT validate units (lines 79–81, 96–98, 110–112) but fractional_exitance and band_radiance_tophat (lines 121–175) accept metres/celsius and return plausible nonsense (0.0), contradicting the docstring of _validate (lines 38–42) and skill line 37–38.

ir-radiometry skill line 109 says to express the LUT-vs-quadrature tolerance in mK; skill line 76 gives the quadrature-vs-closed-form check as 0.1 %; the ship-step commit example (line 83) claims 'agrees with direct Simpson quadrature to < 2 mK' — 0.1 % of Lb(300 K, 7.5–13.5 µm) is ~63 mK, so the two checks cannot be the same test and the example's 2 mK cannot come from the 0.1 % top-hat comparison.
